quizName: DMV Practice Test #7 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Which of the following provides the best protection?
questions.explanation: A plastic face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not enough protection.

questions.question: Small vehicles can appear ______ and seem to be traveling ______ than they actually are.
questions.explanation: Small vehicles like motorcycles can look farther away and slower than they really are. This makes it hard for other drivers to judge their true distance and speed.

questions.question: Goggles can:

options.text: Protect your eyes and your face.
Protect your face but not your eyes.
Protect your eyes, but not your face.
Not protect your face or eyes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect your eyes, but not your face.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes only. Only a face shield can protect your entire face during a crash.

questions.question: Reflective material on your helmet:

options.text: Should only be used at night.
Does not help you to be seen.

questions.explanation: Reflective material on your vest or helmet makes you more visible to other drivers. Use it day and night.

questions.question: If your motorcycle begins to wobble, you should:

options.text: Keep riding, as the wobble will likely correct itself.
Close the throttle to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close the throttle to slow down.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up—this makes the wobble worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle to slow down. Move your weight forward and down. Pull off the road safely to fix the problem.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle:

options.text: The pass may be completed in a no passing zone.
The rider may travel up to 10 mph over the speed limit to complete the pass.
The pass must be started and completed within a passing zone.
The pass must be completed on the shoulder, if one is present.

questions.correctAnswerText: The pass must be started and completed within a passing zone.
questions.explanation: You must start and finish passing only in areas where passing is legal and safe. Always follow the speed limit.

questions.question: Where is the greatest potential for conflict between motorcycle operators and other drivers?
questions.explanation: Intersections are where conflicts between motorcycles and other vehicles happen most often. Be extra careful when approaching and driving through intersections.

questions.question: The front brake:

options.text: Should only be used when you need to stop quickly.
Should be used only under slippery conditions.
Is not as effective as the rear brake.
Is safe to use, if used properly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is safe to use, if used properly.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes when you slow down or stop. The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake and is safe when used correctly.

questions.question: Which formation is best for keeping the riders in a group close together?
questions.explanation: A staggered formation keeps riders close together while giving each rider safe spacing. Use single-file when turning, taking curves, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: A group of riders should pass another vehicle:
questions.explanation: On a two-lane road, riders should pass one at a time. The second rider should wait until the first rider is safely back in the original lane before passing.

questions.question: Where should you get the main information about your motorcycle?

options.text: The person who owned it before.

questions.explanation: The owner's manual is the best source for information about your specific motorcycle. Read it before you ride for the first time.

questions.question: What is good protective gear for a motorcyclist?

options.text: Shoes that stop below the ankle.

questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs completely. Wear boots or shoes that cover and support your ankles with low heels. Leather gloves or other durable material protect your hands and give you a better grip on the controls.

questions.question: What should you do to be more visible to other drivers?

options.text: Turn off your headlight during the day.
Keep your headlight on at all times.
Ride in the right part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your headlight on at all times.
questions.explanation: To be more visible, wear bright and reflective clothes, keep your headlight on at all times, and change your lane position as needed.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks can your body eliminate per hour?
questions.explanation: Your body eliminates about one drink per hour on average. The time it takes can vary. Do not ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: What can cause the front wheel and handlebars to shake or wobble?

options.text: Brakes that are not working properly.

questions.explanation: Wobbling is usually caused by improper loading, unsuitable accessories, or incorrect tire pressure.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What is a danger of braking too hard?

options.text: Losing traction on one or both wheels.
Coming to a complete stop before you expect to.

questions.correctAnswerText: Losing traction on one or both wheels.
questions.explanation: If you brake too hard, you may lose traction on one or both wheels and crash.

questions.question: If your motorcycle weaves over rain grooves or bridge gratings, what should you do?

options.text: Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
Grip the handlebars tighter and speed up to cross it quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Weaving over rain grooves or bridge gratings is usually not dangerous. Simply relax and ride straight across at a steady speed. Zigzagging is more dangerous than riding straight.

questions.question: When you carry a passenger or cargo, what happens?

options.text: You accelerate faster, but stop slower.
You accelerate slower and stop slower.
You accelerate slower, but stop faster.
You accelerate faster and stop faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: You accelerate slower and stop slower.
questions.explanation: Extra weight from a passenger or cargo makes your motorcycle take longer to accelerate and stop.

questions.question: Why should you use both the front and rear brakes when you slow down or stop?

options.text: Using one brake causes uneven wear.
It builds good braking habits for emergencies.
It is the only way to slow a motorcycle.
The brakes only work when both are used.

questions.correctAnswerText: It builds good braking habits for emergencies.
questions.explanation: Using both brakes during normal stops helps you form a habit of always using both. This habit is important in emergencies when using both brakes may be critical.

questions.question: When riding in fog, what should you do?

options.text: Switch between low and high beams.

questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect off the fog and make it harder to see. Do not use high beams when other vehicles are nearby.

questions.question: When should you keep more space between you and other vehicles?

options.text: When it is colder than usual.
When you are following other motorcycles.

questions.explanation: Keep extra space when roads are wet or icy. This gives you more time to stop if needed. A two-second distance is normal, but increase it when stopping is harder.

questions.question: What does an experienced rider do with lane position?

options.text: Changes positions within their lane as conditions change.
Stays in one portion of a lane at all times.
Weaves within the lane to be more visible.
Travels only on the oily portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Changes positions within their lane as conditions change.
questions.explanation: Motorcyclists can use three different lane positions. Choose the safest position based on road and traffic conditions at the time.

questions.question: To see better when passing a vehicle on the left, where should you ride in your lane?

options.text: Ride in the left portion of your lane.
Ride in the right portion of your lane.
Ride in the center portion of your lane.
Try to stand up on your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the left portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane before passing. This helps you see ahead better and makes you more visible to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What should riders do when changing lanes?

options.text: Rely only on their mirrors to identify other vehicles.
Turn their head to look for traffic behind them.
Slam on the brakes to allow any vehicles in their blind spot to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn their head to look for traffic behind them.
questions.explanation: Always turn your head to check for traffic before changing lanes. Motorcycles have blind spots, so mirrors alone are not enough.
